transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um... I guess I'm here because work has been getting harder lately. I'm an accountant, and... well, I keep starting things and not finishing them. Like follow-up items after audits, or mentorship events. I start them, and I fully intend to finish them, but then days later I realize the final email or the review note or whatever form it is... just never actually got done. So, yeah. That's why I made the appointment.
Looking back at your childhood or your time in school, did you struggle with staying organized or finishing tasks back then, too?

Um... yeah, I suppose I did. I mean... my mom still jokes about it sometimes. She says I could ace a test but completely forget to turn in a project that was just sitting right there in my backpack. 

So... yeah. Even back in elementary school, my report cards usually said I was bright, but... I guess I lost assignments a lot. Rushed past the small details. Talked out of turn... things like that. I always needed reminders to actually finish my work back then, too.
Do you find that you often feel physically restless, like you have a hard time sitting still for long meetings or during quiet activities?

Yeah, I guess so. Sitting still for... like, a long review or something... it just feels physically uncomfortable. It's almost like this pressure building up inside me. Eventually I just have to stand up, or walk to the printer, or... I don't know, just invent a reason to move around.
Do you find that these difficulties with focus and restlessness happen in your personal life as well, such as when you are at home or socializing, or is it primarily just at work?

Yeah... it happens at home, too. 

Um... at work, it's gotten to the point where... well, a client review got messed up because of my mistakes and not finishing things. I think people are starting to wonder if I can actually handle the promotion I'm up for. 

And at home... my husband basically handles all the bills now. And other things I said I'd do. He just... he can't really count on me to actually get them done. So, yeah. It's not just work.
When you are in those social situations or at home, do you find that you frequently talk excessively or interrupt others when they are speaking?

Um... I suppose. I don't know about talking excessively, but... I do interrupt sometimes. 

Actually, I notice it mostly at work... like with the junior auditors. An answer or an idea will just feel really urgent in my head, and... I catch myself jumping into the conversation before they can even finish. I just kind of blurt it out before I can stop myself. So... yeah, I guess I do that.
Would you say that your need to move around or your tendency to interrupt others happens on a daily basis, or does it only occur occasionally?

Um... I'm not really sure. I don't really keep track of it, to be honest. 

I don't know if it's every single day, exactly... it just happens sometimes. I haven't really thought about the exact frequency.

Have these difficulties with focus and restlessness caused you significant problems in more than one area of your life, such as in your marriage or your social relationships, in addition to the issues at your job?

Um... I mean, I already told you about work, and... my husband having to take over the bills. I don't really know if I'd call it a significant problem in my marriage, it's just... what I said before. And socially... I don't know. I haven't really noticed anything else.
Looking back at your childhood, would you say that this tendency to feel restless and interrupt others was present then as well, or is that something that has only developed more recently?

Um... I guess so. It's been there a while. 

I mean... even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I would lose assignments or rush through things and miss details. And, um, they said I talked out of turn a lot. Needed reminders to finish my work. 

My mom actually still jokes about it sometimes... she says I could get an A on a test but completely forget to turn in the project that was sitting right there in my backpack. So... yeah, I suppose it's not new.

Looking at your life as a whole, would you say that the physical restlessness and the tendency to interrupt others have been a consistent, persistent pattern for you since childhood, or do those behaviors tend to come and go?
Um... I don't know. I guess it's just always been there. I haven't really thought about whether it comes and goes... it's just how I am, I suppose.
Looking back, would you say that your difficulties with staying focused and finishing tasks have been more of a struggle for you than the physical restlessness and the tendency to interrupt others?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't tried to compare them like that. They both just... happen, I guess. I don't know if one is worse than the other.
When you think about the times you feel the need to move around or interrupt others, would you say these behaviors occur very frequently—almost every day—in multiple different settings?
Um... I don't really keep track of it like that. I'm not sure if it's every single day, or... everywhere I go. I just... I haven't really paid that much attention to the exact timing of it all.

When you are in situations where you are expected to sit still for long periods, such as during a movie or a long dinner, do you find it nearly impossible to remain seated without feeling a strong, almost overwhelming urge to get up?

I mean... I guess. When I have to sit through a long audit review or something, it just... it gets really uncomfortable. Like this pressure just builds up inside until I... I don't know, I just have to stand up. I'll go to the printer or just... find some reason to move.

If you had to choose which one causes you more trouble in your daily life, would you say it is the difficulty with focus and finishing tasks, or the physical restlessness and tendency to interrupt others?
I... I don't really know how to choose between them. I haven't really thought about it like that. They both just kind of... cause problems, I guess. I'm not sure which one is worse.

When you reflect on your daily life, would you say that you find yourself fidgeting, squirming, or feeling the need to be 'on the go' in almost every situation where you are expected to be still, or does this mostly happen only during those specific work meetings?

I suppose it's not just work. Even on weekends... I'll tell my husband I'm just going to rest. But then I'm doing laundry, checking emails, going for a run, trying to plan volunteer stuff... I don't really stop until I'm just exhausted. So, I guess it happens at home, too.

When you think about the times you feel the need to move around, talk out of turn, or interrupt others, would you say these behaviors happen frequently enough that they are clearly noticeable to your friends or family members on a regular basis?

I mean... probably. I know they notice at work, at least. Like... when I'm dealing with the junior auditors. I catch myself jumping into the conversation before they even finish. It's just... the answer or the idea feels really urgent in my head, and I end up blurting it out before I can stop myself. So, yes... people probably see that.

If you had to look at your life as a whole, would you say that your struggles with inattention—like losing things or failing to finish tasks—are just as frequent and disruptive as your physical restlessness and tendency to interrupt others, or do you feel that the restlessness and impulsivity are the more dominant issues?
I... I don't really know. I haven't measured them against each other. They both just kind of happen. I guess they're both there. I'm not sure if one is worse than the other.
When you are in social situations, do you find that you often feel like you are 'driven by a motor' or that you have to be constantly active in ways that others might find unusual or disruptive?
I don't really know if people think it's unusual. I just... I guess I like to keep busy. I don't really think about feeling like a motor. I just do things.
When you are in situations where you need to wait your turn, such as standing in a line or waiting for your turn in a conversation, do you find it extremely difficult to wait?

I guess I don't like waiting. Like... if I have to go to the courthouse records office for work, or if I'm sitting in a clinic lobby. I just get really tense. I end up checking my phone over and over, or I just sit there rehearsing what I'm going to say when it's finally my turn. It's just hard to just sit there and wait.

Looking back over the past six months, would you say that you have consistently experienced at least six distinct symptoms of inattention—like losing things, being distracted, or failing to finish tasks—and at least six distinct symptoms of hyperactivity or impulsivity—like being unable to sit still, interrupting others, or feeling the need to be constantly on the go?

I don't know if I can count them up like that. I haven't really sat down and tallied six of one and six of the other. I just know I've had a hard time with both sides of it lately... it's just been a struggle. I couldn't give you an exact number, though.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a persistent pattern of inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms that have been present since childhood, leading to functional impairment in both professional and personal domains. The clinical presentation meets the criteria for combined-type ADHD.
